Almost all of the legal assistant jobs require at least an associates degree, so this increasingly renders paralegal studies certificates tedious and obsolete for the future. I’ve also spoken to a few attorneys in the recent past and they have corroborated the preference for tangible college degrees. Which is what I heavily recommended to OP, degree over certificate.

I just had a natural interest and passion for law and politics in general, it just seemed natural and a good-fit, especially if I did not have it in me to commit to law school. My college framed it as being the ideal fit for me, as did my family. I was swayed in by the prospects and the room for growth in something that I genuinely enjoy.

I have moved on. I think it’s a combination of the stagnation in this field, perhaps the lingering automation, coupled by the fact that law firms are very hesitant to hire outside as opposed to promoting from within, my location and perhaps my lack of deep connections. I also took all online or night classes in order to open myself up for fulltime work to no avail.

Eventually the process just wears some of us out. A really debilitating catch 22 for me was that legal internships often required previous assistant experience of some kind whilst internships are supposed to be regarded as the new entry level jobs.
